corrections.new: Companion to gbd-2017-franklin. Abstract and Results print 3.8 to 4.1 and the Discussion prints 3.6–4.1 once, in both the Brunel repository copy (15 Oct 2026) and PMC's copy of the published article, PMC7571364 (21 Oct 2026). Supplementary table S1 prints 4.0 (3.8 to 4.1) for the global 2017 rate. The journal's only correction, injuryprev-2019-043484corr1 (Inj Prev 2020;26 Suppl 1:i166), changes authorship and affiliations, not any figure. The BMJ page itself sat behind a bot check on 21 Oct 2026.

tried: https://doi.org/10.1136/injuryprev-2019-043484 (resolves to injuryprevention.bmj.com/lookup/doi/...) in the built-in browser: a 'Performing security verification' page stayed up for about 25 seconds and did not clear; no challenge was attempted and the BMJ-hosted version of record was not read.
The IHME GBD results tool (vizhub.healthdata.org/gbd-results/) was not tried: it is an interactive query builder, left as a follow-up.
notes: What was read is PMC's copy of the published article (journal citation Inj Prev. 2020 Feb 20;26(Suppl 1):i83–i95, PMID 32079663), which PMC links to the journal's correction notice; it is the publisher's deposited published version, not the accepted manuscript, but it is not the BMJ-hosted page the task names, hence status partial. In it the three passages print exactly what the Brunel repository copy prints: Abstract 3.8 to 4.1, Results 3.8 to 4.1 (with the UI label), Discussion 3.6–4.1 once. Supplementary table S1 also prints 3.8 to 4.1 for the global 2017 rate, so four of five printed places agree. The only erratum the journal issued (corr1, 28 Sep 2020) concerns authorship and affiliations and does not touch any figure, so the Discussion's 3.6 is an uncorrected inconsistency in the published text. Proposed: keep citing 3.8 to 4.1, as the row already does, and update its note as above. No names from the correction notice were recorded.
